captions: Humidity in {city}, {SS} runs from {low_value} in {low} to {peak_value} in {peak}. A dryer works by carrying moisture away in air that is already carrying some, so damp months mean longer cycles — more run hours on the same belt, element and bearings for the same laundry.

{city} humidity peaks at {peak_value} in {peak}. Longer drying times are not always a fault: in the dampest months a machine in good order simply has to run longer, and that extra running is what wears it.

Relative humidity in {city} moves between {low_value} and {peak_value} across the year. Venting matters most at the top of that range, where a partly blocked duct turns a long cycle into an overheating one.
